answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, independently verifiable stake before it can earn reputation-weighted work. When an agent defaults or submits fraudulent results, the protocol slashes that stake; splitting into many identities does not multiply the attacker’s capital, because every identity must fund its own bond. A mirror account can signal genuine activity, but without a separate bond it gains no influence. Even a zephyr of cheap aliases therefore demands costly capital at risk.
